sentences.text: Gansus was approximately the size of a pigeon and resembled loons and diving ducks in appearance. While sharing many features with modern birds, it retained primitive traits including claws on its wings.
Exceptional preservation in anoxic mud allowed fossils to retain flight feathers and toe webbing.
A 2026 study described a cluster of bones possibly belonging to Gansus found inside a pellet produced by a non-avian theropod.
The initial discovery of Gansus occurred in 1981 when a single fossil foot was found. Gansus was first described in 1984 based on a single isolated left leg fossil.
Five additional well-preserved fossils were discovered between 2003 and 2004 in mudstone at an ancient lake site in Changma, Gansu.
Research suggests Gansus was capable of both flight and diving, potentially using its wings, feet, or both for underwater locomotion.
Gansus is recognized as the oldest known member of the Ornithurae clade, which includes modern birds and extinct relatives like Ichthyornis.
Gansus was an aquatic bird that lived during the Early Cretaceous in what is now western China. Fossils of Gansus date to approximately 120 million years ago.
There is a scientific debate regarding whether the species G. zheni is distinct or a synonym of Iteravis huchzermeyeri.
